paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֥א יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶל־בָּנָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ וְאַגִּ֣ידָה לָכֶ֔ם אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־יִקְרָ֥א אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית הַיָּמִֽים׃

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov called unto his sons, and said: gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the latter days.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter opens with the chapter-defining temporal-horizon phrase *be-acharit ha-yamim* ('in the latter days'), one of the HB's most-contested eschatological-framing formulae. The phrase saturates the prophetic and patriarchal cross-corpus (Num 24:14 Bil'am's oracle; Deut 4:30, 31:29 the Mosaic warnings; Isa 2:2 / Mic 4:1 the Zion-pilgrimage oracle; Jer 23:20, 30:24, 48:47, 49:39; Ezek 38:8+16 the Gog oracles; Hos 3:5; Dan 10:14 the most-explicitly-eschatological deployment). Named scholarship splits between (a) a *distant-future-historical* reading (NJPS 'in days to come'; von Rad; Westermann; Hamilton; the temporal-not-eschatological position) and (b) an *eschatological-prophetic* reading (the later Targumic and rabbinic tradition; Talmud Pesachim 56a on Ya'aqov's attempt-to-reveal-the-end; the Qumran 4QFlor reception). The ASV-baseline 'in the latter days' is preserved on the surface; the central entry [`be-acharit-ha-yamim-latter-days-temporal-eschatological-horizon-cross-corpus`](#be-acharit-ha-yamim-latter-days-temporal-eschatological-horizon-cross-corpus) documents both reading-camps as named-scholarship without adjudicating. Sarna (JPS Genesis p. 331) treats the formula here as openly-temporal (not specifically-eschatological in the apocalyptic sense); Westermann similarly. The lens-discipline standard is strict: NO Christian-soteriological eschatological pre-resolution; NO WoH temporal-cycle / cosmological synthesis. The *he'asfu* ('gather yourselves') imperative matches the *hiqqavtzu* of v 2 in a doubled gathering-imperative summons-formula (cf. archaic-Hebrew-poetry conventions per Cross-Freedman 1975).

paragraphs.text: הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְשִׁמְע֖וּ אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אֲבִיכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: Assemble yourselves, and hear, ye sons of Ya'aqov; and hearken unto Yisra'el your father.

paragraphs.commentary: The doubled imperative *hiqqavtzu / shim'u… shim'u el-Yisra'el avikhem* deploys the chapter's first *bnei Ya'aqov / Yisra'el avikhem* name-doubling within a single verse — the cycle-wide name-shift pattern (governed by overlay [`yaaqov-yisrael-name-shift-cycle-wide-pattern-gen49`](#yaaqov-yisrael-name-shift-cycle-wide-pattern-gen49) and its Gen 45/46/48 sibling-overlays) in its most-compressed form. Cross-Freedman (*Studies in Ancient Yahwistic Poetry* 1975) reads the verse as an archaic-poetry strophic introit, the doubled *shim'u* providing the synonymous-parallelism that anchors the oracle as deliberate poetic-utterance distinct from the surrounding prose. The overlay [`doubled-shimu-summons-chiastic-archaic-poetry-gen49`](#doubled-shimu-summons-chiastic-archaic-poetry-gen49) documents the convention without adjudicating between Cross-Freedman's archaic-pre-monarchic dating and Westermann's later-redactional dating.

paragraphs.text: רְאוּבֵן֙ בְּכֹ֣רִי אַ֔תָּה כֹּחִ֖י וְרֵאשִׁ֣ית אוֹנִ֑י יֶ֥תֶר שְׂאֵ֖ת וְיֶ֥תֶר עָֽז׃

i18n.en: Re'uven, thou art my first-born, my might, and the beginning of my strength; the pre-eminence of dignity, and the pre-eminence of power.

paragraphs.commentary:
The opening line of the Re'uven oracle stages the *bekhorah*-status formally before retracting it in v 4. *Re'uven bekhori atah* names Re'uven as the *first-born* (central [`bekhorah-birthright-firstborn-status`](#bekhorah-birthright-firstborn-status)). *Kochi ve-reshit oni* ('my might, and the beginning of my strength') deploys the *on* lexeme in its specifically procreative-virility sense — not generic 'strength' but the firstborn-as-firstfruits-of-paternal-procreative-vigor formula. Cross-corpus the construction recurs at Deut 21:17 (*reshit ono*, the firstborn-double-portion law); Pss 78:51, 105:36 (the firstborn-of-Mitsrayim slain as *reshit onim*); cf. *un* / *aven* / *on* root distribution. Sarna (JPS Genesis p. 332), Speiser (AB Genesis p. 363), Hamilton (NICOT Genesis 18-50 pp. 648-649) all read *on* here as procreative-vigor; the central entry [`reshit-oni-firstborn-virility-procreative-strength-cross-corpus`](#reshit-oni-firstborn-virility-procreative-strength-cross-corpus) anchors. ASV-baseline 'beginning of my strength' preserves the surface ambiguity, with the procreative-virility sense documented in the rationale.

The doubled *yeter se'et ve-yeter az* ('pre-eminence of dignity, and pre-eminence of power') is a hapax doubled-construction, framing the *bekhor*-double-portion in honorific terms before the v 4 *al-totar* ('thou shalt not have the pre-eminence') retraction. The overlay [`yeter-seet-yeter-az-doubled-preeminence-formula-gen49`](#yeter-seet-yeter-az-doubled-preeminence-formula-gen49) documents the doubled-hapax.

paragraphs.text: פַּ֤חַז כַּמַּ֙יִם֙ אַל־תּוֹתַ֔ר כִּ֥י עָלִ֖יתָ מִשְׁכְּבֵ֣י אָבִ֑יךָ אָ֥ז חִלַּ֖לְתָּ יְצוּעִ֥י עָלָֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Boiling over as water, thou shalt not have the pre-eminence; because thou wentest up to thy father's bed: then defiledst thou it — he went up to my couch.

paragraphs.commentary:
The verse retracts the v 3 *bekhorah*-honour with the hapax *pachaz ka-mayim* ('boiling over as water' / 'unstable as water' / 'reckless as water'). The *pachaz*-noun is hapax; the verbal *p-ch-z* root appears Judg 9:4 (Avimelekh's *anashim reqim u-fochazim*), Zeph 3:4 (Yerushalayim's reckless prophets), Jer 23:32. Three named-scholarship reading-camps: (i) *instability/turbulence* (ASV, KJV, classical); (ii) *recklessness/wantonness* (NJPS; modern academic); (iii) *boiling-over/uncontrolled-sexual-impulse* (the reading tied to the Bilhah-incest motive — Sarna, Alter). The overlay [`pachaz-ka-mayim-hapax-instability-recklessness-or-passion-gen49`](#pachaz-ka-mayim-hapax-instability-recklessness-or-passion-gen49) documents the three readings; ASV 'boiling over as water' is preserved on the surface as the rendering closest to the demotion-register.

The motive-clause *ki alita mishk'vei avikha* ('because thou wentest up to thy father's bed') is the verse's explicit cross-reference to the Gen 35:22 Re'uven-Bilhah deed (governed by the existing overlay [`reuben-bilhah-deed-succession-claim-gen-49-retrospective`](#reuben-bilhah-deed-succession-claim-gen-49-retrospective)). 1 Chr 5:1-2 supplies the canonical-HB-internal explicit reception of this verse as the *bekhorah*-transfer trigger.

The mid-verse 3ms verb *alah* ('he went up') breaks from 2ms *alita / chillalta*. Three reading-camps: (a) MT 3ms preserved as a *Ya'aqov-voice-break* — the patriarch turns away from direct-address to a distancing third-person utterance (Cassuto, Speiser, Hamilton, Alter; the literary-shock reading); (b) emendation to 2ms (LXX, Vulgate, Syriac); (c) the *alah* as a textual-corruption marker (some critical readings). The overlay [`alah-third-person-voice-shift-mid-verse-gen49`](#alah-third-person-voice-shift-mid-verse-gen49) documents the MT-preserved literary-shock reading.

The *firstborn-priority-reversal-irony* central pattern reaches its narrative-payoff here: the verse explicitly articulates what Gen 48 staged through the hand-crossing. The Gen 48-editor-report flagged this as a *consequence-locus* deployment; the central [`firstborn-priority-reversal-irony`](#firstborn-priority-reversal-irony) appliesTo is extended here.

paragraphs.text: שִׁמְע֥וֹן וְלֵוִ֖י אַחִ֑ים כְּלֵ֥י חָמָ֖ס מְכֵרֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: Shim'on and Levi are brethren; weapons of violence are their swords.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Shim'on ve-Levi achim* opens the joint-oracle that runs through v 7. *Achim* here carries both literal-fraternal and idiomatic-conspiratorial register — 'brothers in conduct' as much as 'brothers by blood' (Sarna, Alter, Westermann; the pairing recalls the Gen 34 Shechem-slaughter conspiracy). The hapax noun *mekheroteihem* is one of the chapter's principal lexical cruxes; four named-scholarship reading-camps: (a) *swords / cutting weapons* (ASV, Vulgate *gladii*; possibly = Greek *machaira* loanword — the classical reading); (b) *dwellings / habitations* (BDB; Akkadian *mākaru* 'to dwell' cognate); (c) *covenants / compacts* (Akkadian *makāru* 'trade/agreement'; the Shechem-deceit-covenant reading); (d) *plans / counsels / devices* (Speiser's deliberative-evil reading). The overlay [`mekherot-shimon-levi-hapax-fourfold-philological-crux-gen49`](#mekherot-shimon-levi-hapax-fourfold-philological-crux-gen49) documents all four readings without adjudication.

*Kelei chamas* ('weapons of violence' / 'instruments of violence') deploys the *chamas* keyword — the load-bearing theological-violence lexeme that triggered the Flood (Gen 6:11+13 *malah ha-aretz chamas*) and saturates Psalms / prophets / wisdom. The new central [`kelei-chamas-instruments-of-violence-cross-corpus`](#kelei-chamas-instruments-of-violence-cross-corpus) anchors. The Gen 34 Shechem-slaughter is the explicit narrative-precedent (sibling-link to the overlay [`be-mirmah-deception-ya-aqov-cycle-inheritance`](#be-mirmah-deception-ya-aqov-cycle-inheritance) and the broader Gen-34 Shechem-narrative entries in the Genesis-WoH cycle).

paragraphs.text: בְּסֹדָם֙ אַל־תָּבֹ֣א נַפְשִׁ֔י בִּקְהָלָ֖ם אַל־תֵּחַ֣ד כְּבֹדִ֑י כִּ֤י בְאַפָּם֙ הָ֣רְגוּ אִ֔ישׁ וּבִרְצֹנָ֖ם עִקְּרוּ־שֽׁוֹר׃

i18n.en: O my soul, come not thou into their council; unto their assembly, my glory, be not thou united; for in their anger they slew a man, and in their self-will they hocked an ox.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Be-sodam al-tavo nafshi / bi-qhalam al-techad kevodi* ('into their council let not my soul enter / unto their assembly, my glory, be not united') deploys the classic synonymous-parallelism of archaic-Hebrew-poetry. *Sod* ('council / secret-circle') paired with *qahal* ('assembly') traces the patriarch's formal-disavowal of the Shim'on-Levi conspiratorial-action.

*Hargu ish / iqqru shor* ('they slew a man / they hocked an ox') is the explicit narrative-recap of the Gen 34 Shechem-slaughter. *Iqqru shor* ('they hocked an ox' / 'they hamstrung an ox') deploys the Piel of *aqar* ('to disable by cutting the hamstring'); cross-corpus Josh 11:6+9, 2 Sam 8:4, 1 Chr 18:4 (the war-practice of hamstringing horses). The *shor* ('ox / bull'): literal (a Shechemite ox they disabled) vs metonymic (the Shechemite men as 'oxen' / 'bulls' in a metaphor of strong-men disabled). Some witnesses read *shur* ('wall'); LXX *tauros* preserves the literal. The overlay [`iqqru-shor-shechem-slaughter-echo-literal-or-metonymic-gen49`](#iqqru-shor-shechem-slaughter-echo-literal-or-metonymic-gen49) documents the literal-vs-metonymic crux and the *shor*/*shur* textual variant; ASV 'they hocked an ox' is preserved.

paragraphs.text: אָר֤וּר אַפָּם֙ כִּ֣י עָ֔ז וְעֶבְרָתָ֖ם כִּ֣י קָשָׁ֑תָה אֲחַלְּקֵ֣ם בְּיַעֲקֹ֔ב וַאֲפִיצֵ֖ם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel: I will divide them in Ya'aqov, and scatter them in Yisra'el.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Arur appam ki az / ve-evratam ki qashatah* ('cursed be their anger, for it was fierce / and their wrath, for it was cruel') deploys the *arur* curse-formula — one of the corpus's load-bearing curse-utterances (Gen 3:14+17 serpent-and-ground; Gen 4:11 Cain; Gen 9:25 Kena'an; Gen 27:29 the Yitzchaq-blessing curse-blesser-formula; Deut 27-28 the Mt-Ebal *arur*-cluster). The new central [`arur-curse-formula-patriarchal-utterance-cross-corpus`](#arur-curse-formula-patriarchal-utterance-cross-corpus) anchors; the formula's deployment here against the patriarch's-own-sons's *anger* (not the sons themselves) is editorially-careful — the curse names the affect, not the person.

*Achalqem be-Ya'aqov va-afitzem be-Yisra'el* ('I will divide them in Ya'aqov, and scatter them in Yisra'el') is the dispersal-prophecy. Its HB-internal fulfilment: Shim'on absorbed by Yehudah (Josh 19:1+9 — Shim'on's territory *within* Yehudah's portion); Levi as priest-tribe-without-territory (Num 18:20+24; Deut 18:1-2; Josh 21 the Levitical cities scattered through the other tribes). The new central [`achalqem-afitzem-shimon-levi-dispersal-prophecy-and-hb-internal-fulfilment-gen49`](#achalqem-afitzem-shimon-levi-dispersal-prophecy-and-hb-internal-fulfilment-gen49) anchors and documents the Josh-Num cross-corpus fulfilment-record.

paragraphs.text: יְהוּדָ֗ה אַתָּה֙ יוֹד֣וּךָ אַחֶ֔יךָ יָדְךָ֖ בְּעֹ֣רֶף אֹיְבֶ֑יךָ יִשְׁתַּחֲוּ֥וּ לְךָ֖ בְּנֵ֥י אָבִֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: Yehudah, thee shall thy brethren praise: thy hand shall be on the neck of thine enemies; thy father's sons shall bow down before thee.

paragraphs.commentary:
The verse opens the central Yehudah oracle (vv 8-12) with the *Yehudah / yodukha* paronomasia on the *y-d-h* root — the editorial-recurrence of the Gen 29:35 name-aetiology (*ha-pa'am odeh et-YHWH al-ken qare'ah shemo Yehudah*, Le'ah's naming-formula). The overlay [`yehudah-yodukha-name-paronomasia-recurrence-gen49`](#yehudah-yodukha-name-paronomasia-recurrence-gen49) documents the chapter-internal name-pun.

*Yadekha be-oref oyveikha* ('thy hand shall be on the neck of thine enemies') deploys the warrior-formula of victory; cross-corpus Ps 18:41 / 2 Sam 22:41 (David's same construction). *Yishtachavu lekha bnei avikha* ('thy father's sons shall bow down before thee') deploys the *hishtachavah* obeisance-formula (existing central [`hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship`](#hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship)). The Yehudah-as-elder-brother-receiver-of-obeisance reading reverses the Gen 37 Yosef-cycle pattern (where the brothers' obeisance was to Yosef): the chapter quietly transfers tribal-leadership from Yosef to Yehudah, consistent with the Gen 46:28 *Yehudah-sent-before* leadership-pattern overlay.

paragraphs.text: גּ֤וּר אַרְיֵה֙ יְהוּדָ֔ה מִטֶּ֖רֶף בְּנִ֣י עָלִ֑יתָ כָּרַ֨ע רָבַ֧ץ כְּאַרְיֵ֛ה וּכְלָבִ֖יא מִ֥י יְקִימֶֽנּוּ׃

i18n.en: Yehudah is a lion's whelp; from the prey, my son, thou art gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as a lioness; who shall rouse him up?

paragraphs.commentary: The Yehudah-lion-cluster: *gur aryeh* ('lion's whelp') / *aryeh* ('lion') / *lavi* ('lioness' or archaic 'lion'). Three lion-words in two consecutive verses (v 9-10 transition). *Lavi* in archaic-Hebrew-poetry is variously read as the gender-feminine 'lioness' or as an archaic high-register masculine 'lion' (Cross-Freedman 1975 on the archaic Phoenician/Ugaritic cognates). *Mi yeqimennu* ('who shall rouse him up?') is the rhetorical-question rousing-formula, echoed at Num 23:24 and Num 24:9 (the Bil'am oracles — the parallel rhetorically explicit there). The new central [`yehudah-aryeh-lion-tribal-emblem-cross-corpus-and-reception-history`](#yehudah-aryeh-lion-tribal-emblem-cross-corpus-and-reception-history) documents the lion-cluster's Genesis-internal observation, the cross-corpus tribal-emblem distribution (Num 23-24 the Bil'am-oracle parallels; Deut 33:7 the Mosheh-Yehudah blessing; 1 Sam-Kings the Davidic-monarchic lion-tradition; Mic 5:7; Hos 5:14 etc.), AND the post-canonical reception layers (the rabbinic/Targumic tradition reading the lion as the Davidic-Messianic emblem; the Rev 5:5 'Lion of the tribe of Yehudah' Christian-apocalyptic reception named-but-not-adjudicated). **STRICT lens-discipline**: NO Christian-Christological adjudication; NO WoH messianic-emblem synthesis.

paragraphs.text: לֹֽא־יָס֥וּר שֵׁ֙בֶט֙ מִֽיהוּדָ֔ה וּמְחֹקֵ֖ק מִבֵּ֣ין רַגְלָ֑יו עַ֚ד כִּֽי־יָבֹ֣א שילה [שִׁיל֔וֹ] וְל֖וֹ יִקְּהַ֥ת עַמִּֽים׃

i18n.en: The sceptre shall not depart from Yehudah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the obedience of the peoples be.

paragraphs.commentary:
**THE CHAPTER'S CENTRAL CRUX — and one of the most-debated single verses in the entire Hebrew Bible.** *Lo-yasur shevet mi-Yehudah u-mechoqeq mi-bein raglav ad ki-yavo Shiloh ve-lo yiqqehat ammim* ('the sceptre shall not depart from Yehudah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the obedience of the peoples be'). The ASV-baseline 'until Shiloh come' (MT proper-name preserved) is the surface; the new central [`shiloh-crux-yehudah-sceptre-philological-and-reception-history-cross-corpus`](#shiloh-crux-yehudah-sceptre-philological-and-reception-history-cross-corpus) documents FOUR philological options AND THREE reception-history layers as named-scholarship-apparatus only without adjudicating.

The four philological options: (a) MT proper-name *Shiloh* — 'until Shiloh come' (the Ephraimite city, Josh 18:1 / 1 Sam 1-4 / Jer 7:12-14; the city's destruction in Jeremiah's day is problematic since the Yehudah-sceptre is not depicted as ending then); (b) *shi-lo* = *that-which-is-his* (re-pointing as *shay* + 3ms-suffix; 'until that which is his comes' — the dominant modern-academic reading, Speiser AB Genesis pp. 365-366; Westermann Genesis 37-50 pp. 222-223; Hamilton NICOT Genesis 18-50 pp. 657-660; Sarna JPS Genesis pp. 336-337; NJPS marginal); (c) *shay lo* = *tribute to him* (LXX *ta apokeimena auto* 'the things laid up for him'; Heb 7:14 partial-echo; Targum Onqelos and Pseudo-Jonathan's *until the Mashiach comes whose is the kingdom*); (d) *shiloh* as variant of *moshel* 'ruler' (S. R. Driver's reading; some Samaritan and Qumran 4Q252 witnesses).

The three reception-history layers, all documented as **named-scholarship-only with explicit operational disavowals**: (i) **Christian-messianic-typological reception** — Justin Martyr's *Dialogue with Trypho* 52-53; Tertullian *Adversus Judaeos* 9; Aquinas; the entire patristic-and-medieval Christian-Jewish-disputation literature; the Reformation and post-Reformation Christian commentary tradition treating this as a Christological prooftext. The reception is named as a *fact of reception-history*; the entry **explicitly disavows Christian-soteriological-Messianic pre-resolution as the controlling interpretation** of the verse. (ii) **Jewish-messianic Targumic reception** — Targum Onqelos *ad d'yeitei Meshicha de-dileh hi malkhuta* ('until the Mashiach comes, whose is the kingdom'); Targum Pseudo-Jonathan and Neofiti same; Talmud Sanhedrin 98b; Bereshit Rabbah 99:8; Rashi (citing the Targumic Mashiach-tradition); Ramban and the subsequent rabbinic tradition. **Equally disavowed as the controlling pre-resolution** — the rabbinic-Mashiach reading is named as a fact of reception-history without being made the lexical-decision. (iii) **Davidic-monarchic historical-critical reading** — Cross *Canaanite Myth and Hebrew Epic* 1973 ch. 9 on archaic-Hebrew-poetry; F. M. Cross + D. N. Freedman *Studies in Ancient Yahwistic Poetry* SBL 1975; Brueggemann; Sarna; the reading of the oracle as proto-Davidic-court-apologetic ending with the unification under David or terminating at the Babylonian exile.

Additionally: *meChoqeq* ('the ruler's staff' / 'lawgiver') is independently contested (overlay [`mechoqeq-rulers-staff-or-lawgiver-philological-crux-gen49`](#mechoqeq-rulers-staff-or-lawgiver-philological-crux-gen49)); cross-corpus Num 21:18 (the wilderness *be-mechoqeq*), Deut 33:21 (Gad's *cheleq mechoqeq*), Isa 33:22 (YHWH as *mechoqeq*). And *yiqqehat ammim* ('obedience of the peoples') is a hapax noun *yiqqehah* (from *y-q-h* 'obey' per ASV; or a textual emendation candidate *yiqqavu* 'gather'; overlay [`yiqqehat-ammim-obedience-of-peoples-hapax-philological-crux-gen49`](#yiqqehat-ammim-obedience-of-peoples-hapax-philological-crux-gen49)). All three cruxes are independently documented; the ASV-baseline preserves the MT throughout.

**STRICT lens-discipline throughout**: the entry does NOT pre-resolve to any of Davidic, rabbinic-Mashiach, Christian-Messianic, or modern-academic *shi-lo*. The Wheel of Heaven translation does NOT take a position on the verse's referent — the philological cruxes and the reception-history layers are documented as named scholarship; no WoH-distinctive synthesis is introduced.

paragraphs.text: אֹסְרִ֤י לַגֶּ֙פֶן֙ עירה [עִיר֔וֹ] וְלַשֹּׂרֵקָ֖ה בְּנִ֣י אֲתֹנ֑וֹ כִּבֵּ֤ס בַּיַּ֙יִן֙ לְבֻשׁ֔וֹ וּבְדַם־עֲנָבִ֖ים סותה [סוּתֽוֹ׃]

i18n.en: Binding his foal unto the vine, and his ass's colt unto the choice vine; he hath washed his garments in wine, and his vesture in the blood of grapes.

paragraphs.commentary:
The verse extends Yehudah's oracle into viticultural-paradisal imagery: *osri la-gefen iro / ve-la-soreqah beni atono* ('binding his foal to the vine / and his ass's colt to the choice vine'). The construction's surface is paradisal-abundance imagery (vines so abundant the colt can be tethered to one and graze without destroying it; Sarna p. 338; Westermann p. 226). The text-critical features: ketiv עירה (iroh, possibly archaic feminine pronominal-suffix) / Qere עִירוֹ (iro, 'his foal'); similarly sotoh ketiv vs suto Qere ('his garment / robe'). The overlay [`ketiv-qere-iroh-iro-suto-sotoh-gen49-orthographic-archaisms`](#ketiv-qere-iroh-iro-suto-sotoh-gen49-orthographic-archaisms) documents the ketiv as preserving archaic-Hebrew-poetry pronominal-suffix orthography (Cross-Freedman 1975 reading).

*Kibbes ba-yayin levusho u-vedam anavim suto* ('he hath washed his garments in wine, and his vesture in the blood of grapes') — the *bedam anavim* construction is editorially-specific viticultural-imagery. Cross-corpus Deut 32:14 (the Song of Mosheh's *dam-enav* — 'blood of the grape'); Sir 39:26 (the Hellenistic-period viticultural echo). The new overlay [`bedam-anavim-blood-of-grapes-viticultural-imagery-and-reception-gen49`](#bedam-anavim-blood-of-grapes-viticultural-imagery-and-reception-gen49) documents the literal-viticultural reading (Yehudah's wine-country tribal-territory in the Yehudah hill country — Hebron, Beit-Tzur, Halhul) AND the figurative/messianic-warrior-readings receivable in named scholarship (the Targumic readings; the Christian-apocalyptic Rev 19:13 'a vesture dipped in blood' + Isa 63:1-6 winepress-judgment reception — named-but-NOT-adjudicated). **STRICT lens-discipline**: NO Christian-apocalyptic pre-resolution; NO WoH winepress-judgment synthesis.

paragraphs.text: חַכְלִילִ֥י עֵינַ֖יִם מִיָּ֑יִן וּלְבֶן־שִׁנַּ֖יִם מֵחָלָֽב׃ (פ)

i18n.en: His eyes shall be red with wine, and his teeth white with milk.

paragraphs.commentary: The hapax adjective *chakhlili* ('red' / 'darker than') yields two grammatically-possible opposite-imagery readings: (a) *red with wine* (causative; cf. Prov 23:29 *chakhlilut einayim* 'redness of eyes from drunkenness' — the only cross-corpus support; ASV preserves); (b) *darker than wine* (comparative; the eyes' clarity contrasted with wine). The overlay [`chakhlili-hapax-adjective-red-or-darker-than-wine-gen49`](#chakhlili-hapax-adjective-red-or-darker-than-wine-gen49) documents both. ASV 'red with wine' is preserved as the rendering grounded in the Prov 23:29 cross-corpus.

paragraphs.text: זְבוּלֻ֕ן לְח֥וֹף יַמִּ֖ים יִשְׁכֹּ֑ן וְהוּא֙ לְח֣וֹף אֳנִיּ֔וֹת וְיַרְכָת֖וֹ עַל־צִידֹֽן׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Zevulun shall dwell at the haven of the sea, and he shall be for a haven of ships; and his border shall be upon Tzidon.

paragraphs.commentary: Zevulun's allotment per Josh 19:10-16 does NOT reach the Mediterranean coast (the coastal-strip is Asher's) and does NOT touch Tzidon (which is Phoenician territory far north of any Yisra'elite tribal area). Three named-scholarship reading-camps: (a) the oracle preserves a *source-critical pre-monarchic tribal-tradition* differing from the Josh 19 allotment (Cross *Canaanite Myth and Hebrew Epic* 1973; Cross-Freedman 1975; Albright on archaic-Hebrew-poetry); (b) *prophetic-projection / future-aspiration* (the tribe's aspirational future-territory rather than its actual holding; Sarna; the Targumic tradition); (c) *commercial-extension* (Zevulun's commercial-shipping access to Tzidon's ports rather than territorial possession; Westermann; Wenham). The overlay [`zevulun-allotment-tzidon-geographic-crux-archaic-vs-prophetic-gen49`](#zevulun-allotment-tzidon-geographic-crux-archaic-vs-prophetic-gen49) documents the three reading-camps.

paragraphs.text: יִשָּׂשכָ֖ר חֲמֹ֣ר גָּ֑רֶם רֹבֵ֖ץ בֵּ֥ין הַֽמִּשְׁפְּתָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: Yissachar is a strong ass, couching down between the sheepfolds.

paragraphs.commentary: *Chamor garem* ('a strong ass' / lit. 'ass of bone') — *garem* deploys 'bone' as adjectival qualifier ('strong-boned / sturdy'); cross-corpus Job 40:18 (Behemoth's bones as bronze tubes uses *garmav*). The overlay [`chamor-garem-strong-bony-ass-hapax-construction-gen49`](#chamor-garem-strong-bony-ass-hapax-construction-gen49) documents. *Bein ha-mishpetayim* — hapax dual form; cross-corpus only Judg 5:16 (the Deborah-Song's *bein ha-mishp'tayim* describing Re'uven's indecision at the sheepfolds). Three readings: 'sheepfolds' (ASV; the dominant reading via Judg 5:16); 'saddlebags / pack-baskets' (some moderns reading the dual as the load-saddle on either side of the ass); 'campfires / hearths' (Cross-Freedman archaic-Hebrew-poetry reading per *Studies in Ancient Yahwistic Poetry* 1975). The overlay [`mishpetayim-sheepfolds-or-saddlebags-hapax-form-gen49`](#mishpetayim-sheepfolds-or-saddlebags-hapax-form-gen49) documents.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֤רְא מְנֻחָה֙ כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב וְאֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ כִּ֣י נָעֵ֑מָה וַיֵּ֤ט שִׁכְמוֹ֙ לִסְבֹּ֔ל וַיְהִ֖י לְמַס־עֹבֵֽד׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And he saw a resting-place that it was good, and the land that it was pleasant; and he bowed his shoulder to bear, and became a servant under taskwork.

paragraphs.commentary:
The Yissachar oracle continues: *va-yar menuchah ki tov / ve-et ha-aretz ki na'emah / va-yet shikhmo lisbol / va-yehi le-mas oved* ('and he saw a resting-place that it was good / and the land that it was pleasant / and he bowed his shoulder to bear / and became a servant under taskwork'). *Menuchah* ('resting-place') is a major cross-corpus keyword: Deut 12:9 (the Mosaic *menuchah* promise of the land); Ps 95:11 (the wilderness-rebellion *menuchah*-loss, with Heb 4 reception); Ruth 1:9; 1 Kgs 8:56; Isa 28:12, 32:18, 66:1; cross-corpus saturation. The overlay [`menuchah-resting-place-cross-corpus-keyword-gen49`](#menuchah-resting-place-cross-corpus-keyword-gen49) documents.

*Mas oved* ('a servant under taskwork' / 'forced-labor' / 'corvée-labor') is institutional vocabulary; cross-corpus 1 Kgs 5:27-28 + 9:21 (the Solomonic forced-labor levy); Josh 16:10, 17:13; Judg 1:28-35 (the Canaanite-forced-labor pattern); Deut 20:11. The new central [`mas-oved-corvee-labor-institutional-vocabulary-cross-corpus`](#mas-oved-corvee-labor-institutional-vocabulary-cross-corpus) anchors. The Yissachar critique-reading (descriptive-disapproval of tribal accommodation to settled Canaanite agricultural servitude) is documented in named scholarship (Sarna; Brueggemann; Hamilton).

paragraphs.text: דָּ֖ן יָדִ֣ין עַמּ֑וֹ כְּאַחַ֖ד שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: Dan shall judge his people, as one of the tribes of Yisra'el.

paragraphs.commentary: *Dan yadin ammo* — the editorial name-wordplay on the *d-y-n* 'judge' root, recurrence of the Gen 30:6 name-aetiology (*dananni Elohim*, Rachel's naming-formula). The overlay [`dan-yadin-name-paronomasia-recurrence-gen49`](#dan-yadin-name-paronomasia-recurrence-gen49) — sibling to the v 8 Yehudah-yodukha overlay — documents. The Dan-judge tradition: Shimshon (Judg 13-16) as the paradigmatic Danite-judge; cross-corpus Deut 33:22 (Dan as a 'lion's whelp' in the Mosheh-blessing — parallel to v 9 Yehudah here). *Ke-achad shivtei Yisra'el* ('as one of the tribes of Yisra'el') anticipates the v 28 *shivtei Yisra'el shenim asar* twelve-tribe formula.

paragraphs.text: יְהִי־דָן֙ נָחָ֣שׁ עֲלֵי־דֶ֔רֶךְ שְׁפִיפֹ֖ן עֲלֵי־אֹ֑רַח הַנֹּשֵׁךְ֙ עִקְּבֵי־ס֔וּס וַיִּפֹּ֥ל רֹכְב֖וֹ אָחֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: Dan shall be a serpent in the way, a horned snake in the path, that biteth the horse's heels, so that his rider falleth backward.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Yehi-Dan nachash alei-derekh / shefifon alei-orach / ha-noshekh iqvei-sus / va-yippol rokhvo achor* ('Dan shall be a serpent in the way / a horned snake in the path / that biteth the horse's heels / so that his rider falleth backward'). *Shefifon* is a hapax zoological term. Egyptian and Semitic comparative evidence supports identification with the *cerastes* (Vipera cerastes, the horned-viper of the Egyptian and Levantine desert that ambushes from sand-tracks and strikes at the heels of passing horses). The overlay [`shefifon-cerastes-hapax-egyptian-zoological-identification-gen49`](#shefifon-cerastes-hapax-egyptian-zoological-identification-gen49) documents.

The imagery is deliberate-tactical-ambush: *iqvei-sus* ('horse's heels') as the ambush-zone, with the rider falling *achor* ('backward'). The tactical-ambush register suits the Dan-Shimshon Judges-cycle tradition; named scholarship reads the imagery as preparing the unique YHWH-prayer interjection at v 18.

paragraphs.text: לִֽישׁוּעָתְךָ֖ קִוִּ֥יתִי יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: I have waited for thy salvation, O YHWH.

paragraphs.commentary:
**THE CHAPTER'S ONLY NARRATOR/Ya'aqov-PRAYER INTERJECTION AND THE ONLY YHWH-NAME OCCURRENCE IN GEN 49** — the rest of the chapter uses *El*, *Shaddai*, *Elohim*. *Li-shu'atkha qiviti YHWH* ('I have waited for thy salvation, O YHWH') interrupts the Dan-oracle between v 17 (snake-and-horse ambush imagery) and v 19 (Gad).

The new central [`li-shuatkha-qiviti-yhwh-unique-prayer-interjection-gen49`](#li-shuatkha-qiviti-yhwh-unique-prayer-interjection-gen49) documents three named-scholarship reading-camps without adjudicating: (a) **Ya'aqov pauses the oracle for prayer** (Sarna JPS Genesis p. 340; Alter *Five Books of Moses* p. 295; Westermann pp. 233-234; the literary-observation that the deathbed-patriarch interrupts the formal-tribal-oracle with a brief unconnected prayer; the Targumic-tradition expansion treats this as Ya'aqov pausing-to-await-the-Dan-Shimshon-end-time-deliverance); (b) **narratorial-pious interjection / liturgical-gloss** (Skinner *Genesis* ICC; some critical scholars treat it as a later liturgical-insertion); (c) **Talmudic Sanhedrin 98b / Targum Pseudo-Jonathan messianic-deliverance reading** — Ya'aqov's pause-for-the-Mashiach-deliverance-prayer in the Dan-end-time-vision context (this is the rabbinic-Mashiach tradition); named-but-NOT-adjudicated.

The *shu'ah* ('salvation / deliverance') lexeme is cross-corpus salvation-vocabulary (Pss saturation; Isa 26:1, 52:7; Hab 3:18; etc.). **STRICT lens-discipline**: NO Christian-Christological-soteriological pre-resolution of the *yeshu'ah* lexeme; NO WoH spin on the unique YHWH-name occurrence.

paragraphs.text: גָּ֖ד גְּד֣וּד יְגוּדֶ֑נּוּ וְה֖וּא יָגֻ֥ד עָקֵֽב׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Gad, a troop shall press upon him; but he shall press upon their heel.

paragraphs.commentary: The densest paronomasia in the chapter — fourfold wordplay on the *g-d-d* root: *Gad* (the name) / *gedud* ('troop / raiding-band') / *yegudennu* ('shall raid / press upon him', Qal yiqtol with 3ms-suffix) / *yagud* ('shall raid', Qal yiqtol). Four occurrences in two clauses. The overlay [`gad-gedud-fourfold-paronomasia-gen49`](#gad-gedud-fourfold-paronomasia-gen49) documents. Cross-corpus Hos 6:9 and Hab 3:16 deploy similar *g-d-d* punning. The *aqev* ('heel') closing echoes Dan's *iqvei-sus* at v 17 and the *Ya'aqov / aqev* name-aetiology cluster (Gen 25:26 + 27:36).

paragraphs.text: מֵאָשֵׁ֖ר שְׁמֵנָ֣ה לַחְמ֑וֹ וְה֥וּא יִתֵּ֖ן מַֽעֲדַנֵּי־מֶֽלֶךְ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Out of Asher his bread shall be fat, and he shall yield royal dainties.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Me-Asher shemenah lachmo* — the verse alone (among the twelve oracles) opens with a prepositional-prefix; the construction is read either as (a) chiastic inversion with v 19 preserving the prepositional-flow ('and from Asher…'), or (b) a textual-redactional accident (the mem properly belonging to the end of v 19 as enclitic-mem per Cross-Freedman 1975). The overlay [`me-asher-prefixed-mem-syntax-crux-gen49`](#me-asher-prefixed-mem-syntax-crux-gen49) documents.

*Ma'adannei melekh* ('royal dainties' / 'kingly delicacies') deploys the *ma'adan* lexeme — royal-court-cuisine vocabulary; cross-corpus 1 Sam 15:32 (Agag's *ma'adannot* 'delicacies'); Prov 29:17 (*ma'adannei nafshekha*); Lam 4:5. The overlay [`maadannei-melekh-royal-court-cuisine-vocabulary-gen49`](#maadannei-melekh-royal-court-cuisine-vocabulary-gen49) documents.

paragraphs.text: נַפְתָּלִ֖י אַיָּלָ֣ה שְׁלֻחָ֑ה הַנֹּתֵ֖ן אִמְרֵי־שָֽׁפֶר׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Naftali is a hind let loose: he giveth goodly words.

paragraphs.commentary: MAJOR PHILOLOGICAL CRUX: the same consonants אילה שלחה can be re-pointed (a) as the MT *ayyalah shelu'ah* ('a hind let loose'; the zoological-MT) OR (b) as *eylah shelucha* ('a terebinth shoot/sapling let-loose'; botanical re-pointing — Cross-Freedman 1975 archaic-Hebrew-poetry reading). The two readings produce wholly-different imagery (a freed deer vs a spreading terebinth). Plus the closing *imrei-shafer*: standardly 'goodly words / fair sayings' (ASV); Speiser AB Genesis (zoological-consistent) reads 'lambs / fawns / offspring'; the botanical-consistent reading would yield 'branches / shoots'. The overlay [`naftali-ayyalah-or-eylah-archaic-poetry-zoological-vs-botanical-crux-gen49`](#naftali-ayyalah-or-eylah-archaic-poetry-zoological-vs-botanical-crux-gen49) documents the three named-scholarship reading-camps. ASV preserved.

paragraphs.text: בֵּ֤ן פֹּרָת֙ יוֹסֵ֔ף בֵּ֥ן פֹּרָ֖ת עֲלֵי־עָ֑יִן בָּנ֕וֹת צָעֲדָ֖ה עֲלֵי־שֽׁוּר׃

i18n.en: Yosef is a fruitful bough, a fruitful bough by a fountain; his branches run over the wall.

paragraphs.commentary: **One of the most-cited philologically-opaque verses in Genesis.** Speiser AB Genesis p. 367: 'one of the most baffling passages in the entire Old Testament'. Westermann Genesis 37-50 p. 231: 'irrecoverable'. Skinner ICC similar. The verse contains multiple compounded cruxes: (a) *ben porat* — standard 'a fruitful bough' (ASV; *ben* = 'son' as botanical 'shoot' + *porat* 'fruit-tree / fruitfulness', anomalous in classical Hebrew); alternatives 'son of fruitfulness' (Aramaic-influenced); 'son of a wild ass / colt' (re-pointing as *ben perat*; cf. *pere* 'wild ass'); 'a wild colt' (zoological re-reading per Cross-Freedman). (b) *alei-ayin* — 'by a fountain / spring' (ASV) vs 'eye-catching / by an eye' (literal) vs Egyptian toponym vs 'looked-upon-with-the-evil-eye' (apotropaic). (c) *banot tza'adah alei-shur* — 'his branches (lit. daughters) run over the wall' (ASV; *banot* as branches-metaphor; *shur* = 'wall') vs 'daughters stride upon a wall' (literal-feminine) vs 'daughters strode over to Shur' (Shur-toponym in the Negev). The new central [`ben-porat-yosef-textual-philological-crux-irrecoverable-gen49`](#ben-porat-yosef-textual-philological-crux-irrecoverable-gen49) documents the multiple-reading-camps and the named-scholarship 'irrecoverable' / 'textually-corrupt' position. NO adjudication. ASV preserved as a defensible-baseline rendering.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיְמָרֲרֻ֖הוּ וָרֹ֑בּוּ וַֽיִּשְׂטְמֻ֖הוּ בַּעֲלֵ֥י חִצִּֽים׃

i18n.en: The archers have sorely grieved him, and shot at him, and persecuted him:

paragraphs.commentary: *Va-ymareruhu va-robbu / va-yistemuhu ba'alei chitzim* ('the archers have sorely grieved him / and shot at him, and persecuted him'). The Yosef-cycle suffering-recap is structurally explicit (echoing Gen 37:18-36 the brothers' attack; Gen 39 the false-accusation; Gen 40-41 the prison-confinement). *Ba'alei chitzim* (lit. 'masters of arrows' = 'archers') is figurative — the brothers and the Egyptian-period adversaries collectively. The overlay [`baalei-chitzim-archers-yosef-cycle-suffering-recap-gen49`](#baalei-chitzim-archers-yosef-cycle-suffering-recap-gen49) documents the recap-function.

paragraphs.text: וַתֵּ֤שֶׁב בְּאֵיתָן֙ קַשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַיָּפֹ֖זּוּ זְרֹעֵ֣י יָדָ֑יו מִידֵי֙ אֲבִ֣יר יַעֲקֹ֔ב מִשָּׁ֥ם רֹעֶ֖ה אֶ֥בֶן יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: But his bow abode in strength, and the arms of his hands were made strong, by the hands of the Mighty One of Ya'aqov, (from thence is the shepherd, the stone of Yisra'el,)

paragraphs.commentary:
*Va-teshev be-eitan qashto / va-yafozzu zero'ei yadav* ('but his bow abode in strength / and the arms of his hands were made strong'). The *eitan* ('steadfast / enduring / perennial') + *qeshet* ('bow') pair forms a classical archaic-Hebrew-poetry warrior-construction (Cross-Freedman 1975). *Va-yafozzu* is hapax-or-near-hapax in this sense (cross-corpus only 2 Sam 6:16 of David's 'leaping' before the ark, possibly different root). The overlay [`va-yafozzu-zeroei-yadav-arms-made-strong-philological-gen49`](#va-yafozzu-zeroei-yadav-arms-made-strong-philological-gen49) documents the hapax sense.

*Mi-ydei avir Ya'aqov / mi-sham ro'eh even Yisra'el* ('by the hands of the Mighty One of Ya'aqov / from thence is the shepherd, the stone of Yisra'el'). **MAJOR DIVINE-TITLE CLUSTER.** The Yosef oracle stages the chapter's densest divine-title cluster. The new central [`avir-yaaqov-mighty-one-of-yaaqov-divine-title-cross-corpus`](#avir-yaaqov-mighty-one-of-yaaqov-divine-title-cross-corpus) documents *avir Ya'aqov* — cross-corpus Ps 132:2+5 (David's *avir Ya'aqov* vow); Isa 1:24 (the variant *avir Yisra'el*); Isa 49:26, 60:16 (*avir Ya'aqov* again); Targum Onqelos *Takkifa de-Ya'aqov* ('the Mighty One of Ya'aqov'). The *avir* lexeme's range covers 'mighty / strong / champion / bull' (the bull-imagery is debated by named scholarship — Albright, Cross, Miller on the ANE bull-divine-epithet tradition; the entry documents without adjudicating).

The new central [`ro-eh-even-yisrael-shepherd-stone-of-yisrael-divine-titles-apposition-gen49`](#ro-eh-even-yisrael-shepherd-stone-of-yisrael-divine-titles-apposition-gen49) documents the *ro'eh* ('shepherd') + *even* ('stone') apposition. The *ro'eh* divine-title connects to the existing central [`elohim-ha-ro-eh-divine-shepherd-metaphor`](#elohim-ha-ro-eh-divine-shepherd-metaphor); the *even* ('stone') is the editorially-distinctive title — cross-corpus Ps 118:22 (the stone the builders rejected); Isa 28:16; Dan 2:34-35 (the smashing stone). Post-canonical reception: rabbinic-Jewish messianic-stone tradition; Christian-NT messianic-cornerstone reception (1 Pet 2:6-8; Eph 2:20 — named-but-NOT-adjudicated). **STRICT lens-discipline**: NO Christian-messianic-cornerstone pre-resolution; NO WoH spin on the divine-titles. The text-critical apparatus: some scholars propose emending *mi-sham ro'eh even* to *mi-shem ro'eh ben* ('by-name-of shepherd, son'); Westermann notes the emendation but does not adopt — MT preserved.

paragraphs.text: מֵאֵ֨ל אָבִ֜יךָ וְיַעְזְרֶ֗ךָּ וְאֵ֤ת שַׁדַּי֙ וִיבָ֣רְכֶ֔ךָּ בִּרְכֹ֤ת שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ מֵעָ֔ל בִּרְכֹ֥ת תְּה֖וֹם רֹבֶ֣צֶת תָּ֑חַת בִּרְכֹ֥ת שָׁדַ֖יִם וָרָֽחַם׃

i18n.en: Even by the El of thy father, who shall help thee, and by Shaddai, who shall bless thee, with blessings of heaven above, blessings of the deep that coucheth beneath, blessings of the breasts, and of the womb.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Me-El avikha ve-ya'azrekha / ve-et Shaddai vi-yvarekhekha* ('by the El of thy father, who shall help thee / and by Shaddai, who shall bless thee'). The verse separates *El-of-thy-father* from *Shaddai* with the *ve-et* construction — unusual syntax that has prompted text-critical comment. The existing central [`el-shaddai`](#el-shaddai) covers Gen 49:25 in its appliesTo as the *El Shaddai* compound's last patriarchal-narrative occurrence; the verse's separable-deployment is noted in the rationale.

MAJOR PHILOLOGICAL/LITERARY OBSERVATION: the *Shaddai* / *shadayim* paronomasia. The verse's closing blessing-cluster names *birkhot shadayim va-racham* ('blessings of the breasts, and of the womb'); the *shadayim* ('breasts') phonologically-and-etymologically resonates with the divine-name *Shaddai*. The Cross-Freedman archaic-Hebrew-poetry tradition (Cross *CMHE* 1973 pp. 52-60; Cross-Freedman *SAYP* 1975; cf. Albright 1935 JBL on *Shaddai*-etymology) documents *Shaddai* as deriving from *shad* 'breast' (cf. Akkadian *šadû* 'mountain' / 'breast' — the same root for both) with the verse's paronomasia preserving the etymology. The new overlay [`shaddai-shadayim-paronomasia-archaic-poetry-cross-freedman-gen49`](#shaddai-shadayim-paronomasia-archaic-poetry-cross-freedman-gen49) documents the Cross-Freedman observation as named scholarship — NOT theologically resolved.

The cosmic three-tier blessing-formula: *birkhot shamayim me-al / birkhot tehom rovetzet tachat / birkhot shadayim va-racham* ('blessings of heaven above / blessings of the deep that coucheth beneath / blessings of the breasts and of the womb'). The three tiers — celestial / chthonic-cosmic / human-fertile — match the cosmic-fertility-blessing tradition of Deut 33:13-16 (the parallel Yosef-blessing in the Mosheh-blessing). The new overlay [`cosmic-three-tier-blessing-formula-shamayim-tehom-shadayim-gen49`](#cosmic-three-tier-blessing-formula-shamayim-tehom-shadayim-gen49) documents.

*Tehom* ('the deep') deploys the existing central [`tehom`](#tehom) — the cross-corpus tehom-keyword Gen 1:2 (creation); Pss; prophets. The appliesTo extends here.

paragraphs.text: בִּרְכֹ֣ת אָבִ֗יךָ גָּֽבְרוּ֙ עַל־בִּרְכֹ֣ת הוֹרַ֔י עַֽד־תַּאֲוַ֖ת גִּבְעֹ֣ת עוֹלָ֑ם תִּֽהְיֶ֙ין֙ לְרֹ֣אשׁ יוֹסֵ֔ף וּלְקָדְקֹ֖ד נְזִ֥יר אֶחָֽיו׃ (פ)

i18n.en: The blessings of thy father have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors unto the utmost bound of the everlasting hills: they shall be on the head of Yosef, and on the crown of the head of him that was separate from his brethren.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Birkhot avikha gavru al-birkhot horai* ('the blessings of thy father have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors'). *Horai* is a hapax form (probably from *h-r-h* 'conceive / parent'). Two named-scholarship readings: (a) 'my progenitors / my parents' (ASV; the MT-pointing standard); (b) 'eternal mountains' (emending *horai* to *harerei* 'mountains' via metathesis; supported by some LXX readings and by the immediate-parallel *ad ta'avat giv'ot olam* 'unto the desire of the everlasting hills' which makes geographic-cosmic reference). The mountains-reading parallels Deut 33:15 (the Mosheh-Yosef-blessing's *harerei qedem* 'mountains of old' + *giv'ot olam* 'everlasting hills'). The overlay [`horai-vs-harerei-mountains-philological-crux-gen49`](#horai-vs-harerei-mountains-philological-crux-gen49) documents. ASV-baseline 'progenitors' preserved.

*Ad ta'avat giv'ot olam* ('unto the utmost bound of the everlasting hills') — *ta'avat* contested: 'utmost bound / boundary' (ASV) vs 'desire / longing' (alternative).

*Nezir echav* ('separated / consecrated from his brothers') — *nezir* is proto-Nazirite-vocabulary; cross-corpus Num 6 (the Nazirite institution); Judg 13:5 (Shimshon as *nezir Elohim*); Lev 25:5+11 (the *nazir* grape-cluster vocabulary). Four reading-camps: (i) 'separated' (ASV / standard); (ii) 'consecrated one' (Nazirite-institutional); (iii) 'crowned / prince' (Targumic; *nezir* as 'crown' / 'diadem'); (iv) NJPS 'elect of his brothers'. The overlay [`yosef-nezir-echav-separated-or-consecrated-or-crowned-cross-corpus-gen49`](#yosef-nezir-echav-separated-or-consecrated-or-crowned-cross-corpus-gen49) documents the four camps and the Num 6 / Judg 13 / Lev 25 cross-corpus.

paragraphs.text: בִּנְיָמִין֙ זְאֵ֣ב יִטְרָ֔ף בַּבֹּ֖קֶר יֹ֣אכַל עַ֑ד וְלָעֶ֖רֶב יְחַלֵּ֥ק שָׁלָֽל׃

i18n.en: Binyamin is a wolf that raveneth: in the morning he shall devour the prey, and at even he shall divide the spoil.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Binyamin ze'ev yitraf* ('Binyamin is a wolf that raveneth') closes the twelve oracles with predatory-warrior-imagery. The morning/evening rhetorical structure (*ba-boqer… ve-la-erev*) deploys the merism. Cross-corpus the Saul-Benjamite warrior-tribe tradition (the Sauline kingdom, 1 Sam; the Ehud-Judges-deliverer narrative, Judg 3; the Sheba-ben-Bichri rebellion, 2 Sam 20; the Benjamite-civil-war, Judg 19-21). The overlay [`binyamin-zeev-yitraf-warrior-tribe-saul-benjamite-tradition-cross-corpus-gen49`](#binyamin-zeev-yitraf-warrior-tribe-saul-benjamite-tradition-cross-corpus-gen49) documents the cross-corpus reception.

*Ad* ('prey') is hapax-or-near-hapax in this sense; cross-corpus only Isa 33:23 ('prey of a great spoil'). The overlay [`ad-archaic-prey-noun-hapax-sense-gen49`](#ad-archaic-prey-noun-hapax-sense-gen49) documents the hapax-sense (distinct from *ad* 'eternity / perpetuity'). *Shalal* ('spoil') is major warfare-vocabulary with cross-corpus saturation (Num 31:11; Josh 7:21; 1 Sam 14:30+32; etc.).

paragraphs.text: כָּל־אֵ֛לֶּה שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֑ר וְ֠זֹאת אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֨ר לָהֶ֤ם אֲבִיהֶם֙ וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אוֹתָ֔ם אִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר כְּבִרְכָת֖וֹ בֵּרַ֥ךְ אֹתָֽם׃

i18n.en: All these are the twelve tribes of Yisra'el: and this is it that their father spake unto them and blessed them; every one according to his blessing he blessed them.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Kol-eleh shivtei Yisra'el shenim asar* ('all these are the twelve tribes of Yisra'el') is the chapter's first explicit articulation of the twelve-tribes-of-Yisra'el institutional-political formula. The new central [`shivtei-yisrael-shenim-asar-twelve-tribes-institutional-political-formula-cross-corpus`](#shivtei-yisrael-shenim-asar-twelve-tribes-institutional-political-formula-cross-corpus) anchors. The *shevet* ('tribe / sceptre / staff') is major HB institutional-vocabulary; cross-corpus saturation Num 1-2 (the wilderness census), Num 26 (the second census), Josh 13-19 (the tribal-allotments), Deut 33 (the Mosheh-blessing), 1 Chr 27 (the Davidic tribal-administration), Ezek 48 (the eschatological-restoration tribal-allotment).

The institutional-tribal-status complications: Levi (without territory; priest-tribe by Num 18:20+24 and Deut 18:1-2); Reuven (eastern-Transjordan per Num 32 / Josh 13); Shim'on (absorbed into Yehudah per Josh 19:1+9); Yosef (two-tribes-via-Ephrayim-and-Menasheh per Gen 48:5 — central [`adoption-formula-li-yihyu-ephraim-menasheh-as-reuven-shimon`](#adoption-formula-li-yihyu-ephraim-menasheh-as-reuven-shimon)). The twelve-tribe count is institutionally-fluid: Levi-out + Yosef-as-two yields twelve in Num 1; Levi-in + Yosef-as-one yields twelve here.

The closing-formula *ve-zot asher dibber lahem… va-yvarekh otam… ish asher ke-virkhato berakh otam* ('and this is it that their father spake unto them and blessed them; every one according to his blessing he blessed them') is the editorial-coda framing the foregoing as a unified-blessing-act despite Re'uven and Shim'on-Levi receiving curses-rather-than-blessings. The overlay [`ve-zot-asher-dibber-chapter-closing-editorial-frame-curses-as-blessings-gen49`](#ve-zot-asher-dibber-chapter-closing-editorial-frame-curses-as-blessings-gen49) documents the editorial-harmonization.

paragraphs.text: וַיְצַ֣ו אוֹתָ֗ם וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ אֲנִי֙ נֶאֱסָ֣ף אֶל־עַמִּ֔י קִבְר֥וּ אֹתִ֖י אֶל־אֲבֹתָ֑י אֶל־הַ֨מְּעָרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּשְׂדֵ֖ה עֶפְר֥וֹן הַֽחִתִּֽי׃

i18n.en: And he charged them, and said unto them: I am to be gathered unto my people: bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Efron the Chitti,

paragraphs.commentary:
*Ani ne'esaf el-ammi* ('I am to be gathered unto my people') deploys THE PATRIARCHAL/MOSAIC death-formula. The new central [`ne-esaf-el-ammav-patriarchal-mosaic-death-formula-cross-corpus`](#ne-esaf-el-ammav-patriarchal-mosaic-death-formula-cross-corpus) anchors. Cross-corpus Gen 25:8 (Avraham); 25:17 (Yishma'el); 35:29 (Yitzchaq); 49:29 + 33 (Ya'aqov here, twice); Num 20:24 (Aharon); 27:13 (Mosheh's prefigured death); 31:2 (Mosheh again); Deut 32:50 (Mosheh's actual death). **The project's fifth central-to-central sibling-pair**: bidirectional cross-reference is wired with the existing central [`shakhav-im-avotav-death-formula`](#shakhav-im-avotav-death-formula); the *ne'esaf el-ammav* formula is the older patriarchal/Mosaic register, *shakhav im-avotav* is the Davidic-royal-historian register (especially Kings). The two formulae overlap but are not identical.

The burial-instruction continues with the Makhpelah-cave (existing central [`me-arat-ha-makhpelah-cave-etymology-hebron-tomb`](#me-arat-ha-makhpelah-cave-etymology-hebron-tomb) appliesTo extends here).

paragraphs.text: בַּמְּעָרָ֞ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר בִּשְׂדֵ֧ה הַמַּכְפֵּלָ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־פְּנֵי־מַמְרֵ֖א בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן אֲשֶׁר֩ קָנָ֨ה אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה מֵאֵ֛ת עֶפְרֹ֥ן הַחִתִּ֖י לַאֲחֻזַּת־קָֽבֶר׃

i18n.en: in the cave that is in the field of Makhpelah, which is before Mamre, in the land of Kena'an, which Avraham bought with the field from Efron the Chitti for a possession of a burying-place.

paragraphs.commentary: The Makhpelah-cave-and-field recapitulation. The chapter consolidates the patriarchal-burial-site recital: Avraham bought the field from Efron the Chitti (Gen 23; the *kesef-male* + *kesef-over-la-socher* legal-transfer formulae); the Mamre-locative anchor (Gen 13:18, 18:1). The existing central [`me-arat-ha-makhpelah-cave-etymology-hebron-tomb`](#me-arat-ha-makhpelah-cave-etymology-hebron-tomb) appliesTo extends. *Achuzzat qaver* ('a possession of a burying-place') deploys the *achuzzah* keyword (existing central [`achuzzah-patriarchal-possession-holding-keyword`](#achuzzah-patriarchal-possession-holding-keyword)); appliesTo extends — the Gen 47:11+27 → Gen 48:4 → Gen 49:30 cycle-cluster reaches its penultimate node here (Gen 50:13 closes).

paragraphs.text: שָׁ֣מָּה קָֽבְר֞וּ אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֗ם וְאֵת֙ שָׂרָ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ שָׁ֚מָּה קָבְר֣וּ אֶת־יִצְחָ֔ק וְאֵ֖ת רִבְקָ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וְשָׁ֥מָּה קָבַ֖רְתִּי אֶת־לֵאָֽה׃

i18n.en: There they buried Avraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Yitzchaq and Rivkah his wife; and there I buried Le'ah:

paragraphs.commentary:
The triple-*shammah* / fourth-*shammah* (*shammah… shammah… ve-shammah*) recital — the chapter's consolidated patriarchal-burial-site account. There they buried Avraham AND Sarah AND Yitzchaq AND Rivkah AND Le'ah.

**The Le'ah-burial at Makhpelah is mentioned ONLY HERE in the corpus.** Gen 35:19-20 records Rachel's burial at Efrat-Beit-Lechem on the road (NOT at Makhpelah; cf. overlay [`efrat-beit-lechem-toponym-davidic-cross-corpus-gen48`](#efrat-beit-lechem-toponym-davidic-cross-corpus-gen48) from the prior chapter's Rachel-grief-recall). The chapter makes the institutional-distinction explicit: Sarah, Rivkah, Le'ah are buried with the patriarchs at Makhpelah; Rachel is buried separately, on the road. The new overlay [`leah-at-makhpelah-rachel-on-the-road-matriarchal-burial-distinction-gen49`](#leah-at-makhpelah-rachel-on-the-road-matriarchal-burial-distinction-gen49) documents — Le'ah as the matriarch-in-the-tomb / queen-matriarch of the Yehudah-and-Levi-line; Rachel as the matriarch-on-the-road / prophetic-grief-matriarch (Jer 31:15 reception).

paragraphs.text: וַיְכַ֤ל יַעֲקֹב֙ לְצַוֺּ֣ת אֶת־בָּנָ֔יו וַיֶּאֱסֹ֥ף רַגְלָ֖יו אֶל־הַמִּטָּ֑ה וַיִּגְוַ֖ע וַיֵּאָ֥סֶף אֶל־עַמָּֽיו׃

i18n.en: And when Ya'aqov made an end of charging his sons, he gathered up his feet into the bed, and yielded up the ghost, and was gathered unto his people.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Va-yekhal Ya'aqov le-tzavvot et-banav / va-ye'esof raglav el ha-mittah / va-yigva va-ye'asef el-ammav* ('and when Ya'aqov made an end of charging his sons / he gathered up his feet into the bed / and yielded up the ghost, and was gathered unto his people'). The chapter closes with a triple-verb death-sequence.

*Va-yigva* — the patriarchal death-verb. The new central [`va-yigwa-expire-patriarchal-death-verb-cross-corpus`](#va-yigwa-expire-patriarchal-death-verb-cross-corpus) anchors; cross-corpus Gen 25:8+17 (Avraham, Yishma'el); 35:29 (Yitzchaq); Num 20:29 (Aharon-related); Job 3:11, 14:10, 27:5; Ps 88:16. The *gawa* root is a documented patriarchal-and-Joban death-verb (Sarna; HALOT; BDB).

*Va-ye'asef el-ammav* — fourth-and-final occurrence of the gathered-to-his-people formula in the death-line (after v 29 *ne'esaf el-ammi*, here v 33 *va-ye'asef el-ammav*); the formula bookends the death-instruction. The new central [`ne-esaf-el-ammav-patriarchal-mosaic-death-formula-cross-corpus`](#ne-esaf-el-ammav-patriarchal-mosaic-death-formula-cross-corpus) governs both verses. The existing central [`shakhav-im-avotav-death-formula`](#shakhav-im-avotav-death-formula) is retained for the sibling-pair register.

*Ha-mittah* ('the bed') — the existing overlay [`mt-lxx-mittah-mateh-bed-vs-staff-textual-variant-gen47`](#mt-lxx-mittah-mateh-bed-vs-staff-textual-variant-gen47) appliesTo extends. The v 33 narrative-action of Ya'aqov *gathering his feet onto the bed* materially reinforces the MT bed-reading against the LXX/Heb 11:21 staff-reading at Gen 47:31 (consistent with the Gen 48:2 *va-yitchazzeq Yisra'el va-yeshev al ha-mittah* sibling-overlay).
